alignments.note: Head noun; split from its article under rule 26.

The ASV gives *faith* no determiner, so this article has no *the* to anchor. Rule 21's determinerless clause makes it `unrepresented` under rule 23 and leaves the case preposition *of* with the noun; rule 21 forbids leaving a bare *of* on the article.
Genitive noun rendered *of faith*; the case preposition rides with the noun per rule 21's determinerless clause, headed on the noun per rule 17.
Future indicative with its auxiliary; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb *save*.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun *him* and nothing else, the relative clause staying with the participle. Rule 90 does not arise, the ASV writing two English words (*him* and *that*) rather than one, so the ordinary split applies; rule 31 does not apply either, since the article governs no expressed head noun.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer and copula are helpers on the participle under rules 7, 9 and 32, headed on the lexical predicate *sick*.

Future indicative with its auxiliary and the phrasal particle *up*, discontinuous across the object pronoun under rule 15; headed on the lexical verb *raise*. The *up* is the English verb's own particle — no Greek preposition stands for it to answer to, so rule 36 does not reach it.
Accusative object pronoun to *him*, kept separate from the verb's own unit.
Subject noun, split from its article under rule 26.

Crasis of `καί` and `ἐάν`: one source word spelling a conjunction and a conditional particle together, so it takes both English words as one `aligned` unit under rule 55. JHN.8.55 is this unit's twin — the same lemma rendered *and if* and headed on *if* — and JHN.11.54 `κἀκεῖ` → *and there* heads on the adverb, which is what shows rule 55's head generalizes past the pronominal to whichever element is not the `καί`. All six corpus `κἄν` units are one `aligned` unit, none `noncompositional` and none split, and of the sixty-three crasis units in the corpus not one is headed on the word answering to the `καί`. This is an ordinary conditional `ἐάν`, so rule 72 does not arise.

Subjunctive of `εἰμί` in the periphrastic perfect `ᾖ πεποιηκώς`; it carries the person and number, so the supplied subject *he* and the auxiliary *have* that realizes it belong here under rules 7 and 9, while the lexical participle keeps *committed*. Reading the two source tokens as one unit on *have committed* is defensible, but rule 2 prefers the split since both English pieces remain independently recoverable.
Perfect participle to the lexical verb *committed*.
Future passive with its supplied subject and auxiliaries; rule 17 heads on the lexical predicate *forgiven*, not on *shall* or *be*.

review_notes: Returned unchanged: the accepted alignment survives review. Every s001-s019 and t001-t029 id is partitioned exactly once; all heads are members of their arrays and the sole `unrepresented` unit (s004) has an empty target and a null target head.

s007/s008 audited against rules 31, 32 and 90. The article governs no expressed head noun, so it is substantival and rule 31 is out; the ASV writes two English words across the pair (*him* and *that*), so rule 90's one-word case is out and rule 32's ordinary split stands - *him* to the article, *that is sick* to the participle headed on the lexical predicate.

s014 `κἂν` stays one `aligned` unit on *and if* under rule 55. Rule 39 is the competing reading and does not carry: it is scoped to a particle fused with the negative `μή`, and here each English word answers to one fused element, which is exactly rule 39's own test for staying `aligned`. Rule 55's head-on-the-pronominal has nothing to select here, so rule 17 decides and puts the head on *if*.

s016/s017 is the one materially contested unit and its note names the alternative: joining `ᾖ πεποιηκώς` into a single unit on *have committed*. Kept split under rule 2, with *he have* on the finite copula that carries the person and number and *committed* on the lexical participle. A later reader wanting to revisit JAS.5 periphrastics should start there.

s005 `πίστεως` -> *of faith* keeps the case preposition on the noun and leaves s004 `unrepresented`, per rule 21's determinerless clause read with rule 23. This is the correct grouping rather than a convenience merge of article and noun, which rule 13 forbids.

s010's *up* is kept with `ἐγερεῖ` as the English verb's own particle, discontinuous across the object pronoun under rule 15. Rule 36 does not apply, since no Greek preposition governs a phrase for it to realize.

No rule 37, 97 or 103 case arises: no token's English sits in a neighbouring verse, the packet marks no excluded fallback, and no supplied English lexical content repeats an already-spent source token. Nothing here is `added`.
